guide.configureRootsEnableFileManagementAndCho: Set up libraries, file management and comic folders
guide.aLibraryIsAMountedServerRoot: A library is a mounted server root
guide.lumaReadsExistingMediaInDirectoriesMount:
A library is a folder mounted on your Luma server. Albums are the folders inside it. Use container paths in your configuration, rather than paths from the host.

To add a disk or share, mount it, add a library in the server configuration and restart Luma.
guide.useConsecutiveConfigurationIndexesStarti:
Start configuration indexes at 0 and keep them consecutive. Give each library a unique ID and keep that ID when upgrading.

Open the library to choose how to scan it. A read-only mount is enough for browsing, tagging, playback and captions.
guide.dockerEnvironmentThenSettingsGeneralFile: Docker environment, then Settings → General → File management
guide.turnOnEnableFileManagementInSettingsGene:
Turn on Enable file management in Settings → General → File management. Each editable library needs Writable=true and a :rw media mount.

The switch is saved for everyone on this server. Luma__Files__Enabled sets its initial value; a saved choice takes priority. No administrator token is needed.
guide.startupBannerSettingsGeneralFileManageme: Startup banner / Settings → General → File management
guide.lumaChecksWriteAccessAtStartupAndWhenEna:
After fixing a mount or its permissions, choose Check media mounts in Settings. Check the result for each library to see which ones have write access. Browsing and tagging still work on read-only libraries.

The brief startup notice has the same details in Settings. Dismissing it hides it until the server next starts.
guide.theEmptyStartPageHasAddComicLocationIt:
In Panels, choose Add comic location or Comic locations. Pick a library, then use Choose folder to browse it. You can browse folders before they’ve been indexed; folder search uses the index. Leave the path empty to use the library root.

Choose Save locations and scan to search that folder and its subfolders. Follow the scan in Background jobs. To include image folders as comics, tick Treat folders containing images as comics. Read-only mounts work too.
guide.checkedByDefaultForEachComicLocationIncl:
Comic locations are excluded from Gallery by default. Their images stay out of Gallery, tag collections and XMP exports. Existing tags and reading progress are kept.

Uncheck Exclude from Gallery to show the images again, then rescan to pick up files added while excluded. If comic locations overlap, a checked parent location still hides its contents. Manually hidden folders stay hidden.

For deployment defaults, use Luma__Panels__Sources__0__ExcludeFromGallery. Saved locations take priority. Configure separate server libraries with non-overlapping roots.
guide.thePanelsStartPageShowsUpToFiveRecently:
Continue reading has your five most recently opened, unfinished comics. Below it are your saved locations, with folder covers in the style chosen in Settings. Open a location to browse its subfolders and books; use Up or Bookshelf to go back.

Search by title, author or series, and filter by reading status, favourite or comic tag. On the bookshelf, search covers all locations. Inside a library, it covers that library. Edit tags from Details. Comic-only tags stay out of Gallery.

Manage locations from Comic locations. Removing a location hides its books but keeps their details and reading progress.
guide.galleryIsAlwaysAvailableEnableOrHideFlic:
Open Settings from the gear in the header. Under General → Applications, choose whether Flick and Panels are available to everyone on this server. Both start enabled.

Saved choices take priority over Luma__Ui__FlickEnabled and Luma__Ui__PanelsEnabled. Back returns to the app you came from.
guide.backUpSQLiteAndOriginalStagingTrashMedia: Before upgrading, stop Luma and back up the database together with your media, staging and trash folders. To roll back, restore that matching backup and the older Luma image.
guide.switchApplicationsManageWritableLibrarie: Apps, file management, uploads and recovery
guide.clickTheLumaLogoToChooseGalleryFlickOr: Click the Luma logo to choose Gallery, Flick or Panels. The small icon beside it marks your current app. Each app remembers its own search and filters.
guide.searchComicTitlesOrSeriesFilterBySeriesC:
Open a comic to continue reading. Use Details to edit its title, series, author, description, favourite status, tags or cover.

Reader settings has page layout, reading direction, fit, zoom and fullscreen. Pinch to zoom and drag to pan. Tap the page counter to enter a page number or use the slider. Swipes, arrow buttons and keyboard shortcuts work too.

Your page is saved automatically, including on HTTP LAN addresses. Use Exit reader when you’re done.
guide.galleryInsideAConfiguredWritableLibrary: Gallery, inside a configured writable library
guide.useTheFileManagementIconBesideSelectToRe:
Click the file-management icon beside Select. Select files or folders, choose Cut or Copy, open a destination folder in the same library and choose Paste. Rename works with one selected item. New folder and Upload use the folder you have open.

For an existing destination, choose Replace or Skip, for one item or all remaining conflicts. Replace sends the old item and its contents to the recycle bin; folder contents aren’t merged. You can cancel while waiting for a busy path.

Delete sends items to the recycle bin unless you choose permanent deletion. The viewer and Flick menus also have Delete; Gallery’s viewer has Rename too. After deleting, you can keep viewing the next item. File management works in search and tag results as well.

Check Background jobs for progress and failures. Keyboard shortcuts work while file management is open: Ctrl/Cmd+X, C, V and Delete, except in text fields or dialogs. Copy stays on the clipboard after pasting; Cut clears after it’s queued.
guide.theUploadDialogHasChooseFilesChooseFolde:
Choose files or a folder, or drop them into the upload window. Folder structure is kept. You can close the window while uploads run and check progress in Background jobs.

After refreshing the browser, choose the same files to resume. For an existing destination, choose Replace or Skip.
guide.restoreOrPermanentlyRemoveRecycledItems: Restore or permanently remove recycled items
guide.chooseAWritableLibraryShowsOriginalPaths:
Choose a writable library to see deleted items, their original paths and deletion dates. Restore puts an item back where it was. If that path is occupied, enter another path within the library.

Items stay in the recycle bin until you delete them permanently, and still take up disk space. Keep a separate backup.

Use a matching external SRT file or an embedded SubRip/SRT track. Turn CC off to hide captions.

guide.forMovieMkvOrMovieMp4PlaceMovieSrt:
Put movie.srt beside movie.mkv or movie.mp4. Uppercase .SRT works too. Language suffixes such as movie.en.srt and files in other folders aren’t matched.

Embedded tracks must use SubRip/SRT. ASS/SSA, PGS/VobSub and MP4 mov_text aren’t supported. Use UTF-8 or BOM-marked UTF-16 text, up to 4 MiB. Luma doesn’t generate subtitles or read them from images.
guide.stylizedSubtitlesAreNotSupportedAuthorFo:
Captions use plain text, without custom fonts, colors, positioning or effects. Temporary and converted subtitle files are kept in Luma’s cache, away from your originals.

If captions fail to load, turn CC off and on to try again.

guide.deploymentPreferenceKeys:
Set a deployment default with Luma__Ui__Preferences__ followed by the preference key. Use string values and quoted objects for JSON settings. Saved choices in the app take priority.

Supported keys: luma-theme, luma-appearance-v2, luma-album-covers, luma-reels-sort, luma-slideshow-seconds, luma-video-autoplay, luma-viewer-fill, luma-reels-fill, luma-show-filters, luma-reels-show-filters, luma-reels-state, luma-panels-reader-defaults.

Boolean settings accept true/false or 1/0; inside JSON, use true or false. Reader defaults apply to comics without saved preferences.
